items.title: the formatter's `assert_formats(source, source)` identity pins are vacuous when the formatter DECLINES — `format` hands the source back on a decline, so a file the printer cannot reprint passes an identity expectation (E252's first pin passed with the bug planted back)
items.discussion: syntax-b-46 (Order 46); REPORT-syntax-b-46.md; E252; N90 (the decline reasons)
items.body: `formatter::reformats::assert_formats` compares `format(source)` with `expected`, and `format` returns the input unchanged when the reprint is declined (does not parse, no rule, the net threw it away). Where `expected == source` — 10 literal calls in `formatter.rs`'s tests, plus loops that feed one variable to both arguments — a decline is indistinguishable from a clean reprint. E252's pin was written that way first and stayed green with the parens planted back; it now asserts through `reprint`, which errs on a decline. Rec: make `assert_formats` assert `reprint(source).is_ok()` first (one line, every caller covered), then read what goes red. Sizing S.

items.title: `return (y);` as a value body's last STATEMENT gets B523's `ret` steer AND "Expected i32, but got void instead: this body ends without producing a value" — the second is true of what was written, and is the cascade B520 avoided for `return value;` by rewriting the token
items.body: B523 steers an unbound `return` where the name fails to resolve (`resolve_prepped_local`); the read becomes `Expr::Error`, but the statement's `;` still leaves the body without a tail, so the return check reports the missing value too. The tail shapes (`return (y)`, `return -x` with no `;`) carry the steer alone. Doors: (a) leave it — both diagnostics are true; (b) let the return check stand down when the body's last statement is an expression statement over an unbound `return` (analyzer, solver's file). Rec: (a) unless it shows up in the editor as noise. Sizing XS.
